label: Tested whether a complete joint cause must account for its indispensable conditions or whether…
summary: Tested whether a complete joint cause must account for its indispensable conditions or whether that demand is a PSR by another name. Findings: a complete record with every contributor supplied can leave a contingent enabler with no record, so closure does not follow from conditional completeness. Demanded of every contingent event, closure with stops at scenario necessity is equivalent to the contingent-fact PSR of the record arena under coherence and memberful records, so in that scope it collapses into a listed form. Demanded of one target it is strictly weaker, unless the target's records list every other contingent event. Closure does not give foundation: chain and cycle models close. Rejected: resting the demand on scenario indispensability, because a one-scenario restriction of the same records removes it and an equal occurrence table with different records changes the verdict. Rejected: treating an SCC as a unit that meets the demand, because condensation gives the cycle component Supply with no intrinsic event while inductive closure fails. No independent justification of the recursive step was found; candidates tried are listed in docs/notes/explanatory-closure-745.md. StoppingPoints (#770) and DerivativeReply (#776) were unmerged at start and not imported.
blocker: Whether closure is demanded of ultimate explanation remains an open normative question, and no premise of it is added. Closure is over listed records, so a defended productive notion of membership is still missing, and bearer existence is not treated. No root premise discharged.
